public.title: Camel Case Keys
public.description: Recursively transform object keys from snake_case to camelCase by replacing each underscore followed by a lowercase ASCII letter with that uppercase letter. Recurse through arrays; preserve scalar values. Transformed sibling keys are guaranteed distinct. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: Transform keys and recursively visit their values, including arrays.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and reference code, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party prose or code copied.

explanation: Rebuild containers while applying the underscore-letter replacement only to keys. Distinct transformed keys avoid collisions. O(total nodes plus key characters) time and output space. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
